title: Resource objects as a Wire authoring/import source
summary: Executable Windows/ooDialog-style resource objects are valuable Builder inputs because they carry structure, occurrence identity and places for triggered events. The recovery bridge maps them into renderer-neutral Wire elements while preserving native resource identity and trigger metadata as provenance.
invariants: Preserve three identities where present: Wire element identity, native/resource ID and resource occurrence UID.
Repeated native IDs such as IDC_STATIC must not collapse distinct occurrences.
Actual bound trigger slots become explicit Wire action bindings; original event/handler names remain inspectable provenance.
Executable handler source is not transported into Web/other renderers merely because the resource object names a handler.
Unknown/custom controls fail closed as a generic RESOURCE_CONTROL rather than disappearing or being guessed.
Win32 resources may feed Wire and Wire may project to resource-compatible forms, but neither resource IDs nor HWNDs become Wire application authority.

provenance.claim: Development/recovery evidence for resource-object to Wire import semantics.
